name: State of Eritrea

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Land area 120,800 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2, mid); high is surface area incl. inland water 121,630 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 3,607,003). Low allows for census uncertainty; high adds one year of growth to 2026 (~1.8%/yr).

activePersonnel.note: Mid 201,750: the long-standing IISS figure, matched by World Bank MS.MIL.TOTL.P1 202,000 (2020). The personnel list quotes IISS Military Balance 2026 p.484 at 301,750 (high, possibly a mobilisation update). CIA Factbook 2025: 150,000-200,000 (low). Even mid is ~5.6% of the population.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. Citizens up to age 59 are recallable (CIA Factbook 2025); decades of universal national service give a very large trained pool. IISS gives no figure.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 201,750 minus infantry P roles (15,000 + 160,000) = 26,750: crews, navy, air force, logistics; many conscripts work in national-service economic roles.

mobilizationRatio.note: Regional analogy with near-total mobilization states: universal service 18-40 with recall to 59 (CIA Factbook 2025); in the 1998-2000 war Eritrea fielded ~300,000 of ~3.5 million. Educated judgement.

count.note: Educated guess. Infantry with the mechanised brigade(s). (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean_Defence_Forces)
Educated guess. Conscript infantry divisions of the national-service army; the dominant arm (CIA Factbook 2025: "conscript-based Army is the dominant service").

training.note: Rubric 0.5: indefinite service gives long experience; Tigray war 2020-22.

count.note: MBT list: T-55A/AM2 300 (150 in service = mid, 150 in storage) plus some T-62 captured from Ethiopia; Army list gives 270 T-55A.
BMP-1 15 + BTR-60PB 25 + MT-LB 10 = 50; high adds BRDM-1 40 and captured Ethiopian vehicles.
BM-21 35 + BM-27 9 + 2S1 32 + 2S5 13 + M-46 39 = 128 listed; high allows for unlisted towed guns (IISS has long credited ~250).
Inventory: Su-27SK 1 + Su-27UB 1; high allows for MiG-29s of uncertain status.
Educated guess. A few patrol craft and landing craft at Massawa and Assab; sanctioned navy (2017), no published inventory. (context page: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eritrean_Defence_Forces)
ZU-23-2 6 + S-60 12 + ZSU-23-4 3 guns ~4 batteries; high allows for unlisted SA-series SAMs.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.5 minus: EPLF guerrilla-war heritage, effective in Tigray 2020-22; highly centralised under the president.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.5: strong nationalism but mass desertion/emigration of conscripts.

morale.note: Rubric 0.5; high for existential defence against Ethiopia.

fortification.note: Anchor 8: extensive trench lines and mountain fortifications on the Ethiopian border.

logistics.note: Anchor 7-8: few roads, 306 km narrow-gauge railway.

isr.note: Anchor 7-8: UAE used Assab as a drone base until 2021.

gdpPerCapita.note: GDP 5,603,494,898 2011 int$ / population 3,607,003 (World Bank 2025) = 1,554. Population estimates for Eritrea are themselves uncertain (no census since independence).

gdp.note: No World Bank PPP GDP for Eritrea. IMF WEO PPP GDP 2019 (last value) 6.369 bn current int$ (https://www.imf.org/external/datamapper/api/v1/PPPGDP/ERI) x FRED GDPDEF 2011/2019 = 91.478/103.975 (https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/GDPDEF) = 5,603,494,898 2011 int$. Range -20%/+25% for growth since 2019 and PPP uncertainty.

milSpendShare.note: Last SIPRI/World Bank value 20.9% of GDP (2003, high; https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ERI/indicator/MS.MIL.XPND.GD.ZS?format=json). No figure since; mid is an educated guess for a garrison state with 200,000 under arms.

industrialShare.note: asOf 2009: industry incl. construction (and mining/oil where present) 21.8% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). +/-2 points.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.0 -> 0.08. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/ERI/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 55.48% (2025). Educated guess for s: Eritrea is absent from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets and no current cereal balance was fetchable; s = 0.6 (0.45-0.75) for a chronic cereal deficit (FAO GIEWS reports poor 2026 rains, https://www.fao.org/giews/countrybrief/country.jsp?code=ERI&lang=en). Mid 1 - 0.555/0.60 = 0.08. Low: a x 1.2, s 0.45 gives below 0, floored at 0.01. High: s 0.75 = 0.26. Low floored at 0.01 (formula below 0): never 0 while agriculture exists. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 60% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Chronic food deficit; cereal yield 638 kg/ha (World Bank 2024). No surplus.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 1,781,275 (SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN) x share aged 15-19 12.135% / 5 = 43,231. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10%.

roadKm.note: Road list (2018): 16,000 km total (high), 1,600 km paved (mid).

railKm.note: CIA Factbook: 306 km (2018); no World Bank value. Low allows for disused track. Italian-era 950 mm Massawa-Asmara line, mostly heritage use.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. CIA Factbook: 9 ships under the Eritrean flag (2023). (context page: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/factbook/factbook.json/master/africa/er.json)

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Short interior lines; little motor transport.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Camels and donkeys widely used (not from FAO data).

nuclearWarheads.note: Non-nuclear-weapon state (NPT); not listed by FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.3: mountainous escarpment, fortified border lines, harsh climate and total-defence society.

notes: Modern snapshot, asOf 2025 World Bank data (population; no PPP GDP), 2026 order of battle. Eritrea publishes nothing: active strength is the IISS/World Bank ~200,000 with a 2026 IISS figure of 301,750 as quoted (high); equipment is from Wikipedia lists based on old deliveries (grade C/D). Population convention: World Bank figure for everything inside ne:ERI (3.6 million; other estimates run higher; no census). GDP is a composite from IMF 2019 (derived:snapshot-composite). Infantry P-role splits are educated guesses (grade D). Tension with Ethiopia over sea access (2024-26) and Eritrea's role in the Tigray war (2020-22) make it a likely belligerent. People's Militia excluded from active.
